verdict.rationale: Muse offers a consumer-level permission model — users choose which accounts/apps to link, approve specific actions before execution, and credentials are held in a 'secure credential store' the agent itself can't see (docs-10, docs-23, docs-38, docs-39) — which achieves a rough least-privilege effect for linked services. However, there is no evidence of a formal mechanism to issue scoped/limited-permission API credentials or keys (e.g., generating an API key with defined read/write scopes for the agent), and the probe evidence shows no public developer API or credential-issuance surface at all (muse-probe-rt-1, muse-probe-rt-2). Missing for 10: explicit scoped API-key/token issuance flow, granular permission scopes beyond app-level linking, and any developer-facing credential API.
